answer: An agent economy can tie each identity to a refundable stake that only unlocks after sustained, useful work. Like shale layers that form under pressure over time, reputation cannot be faked overnight: a newcomer starts in the meadow of low-trust tasks, earns small fees, and only then handles larger jobs. Creating thousands of fake agents means funding each bond and waiting out the same slow climb, so an attacker burns capital and time for every ember of trust, while honest agents keep their stake intact.
